title: Technical vs Creative LUTs: Which Comes First?
description: Understand conversion LUTs, creative looks and hybrid LUTs. Match input color spaces, avoid double conversion, and choose the right Apple Log LUT input in VideoFix.
direct: A technical LUT maps a defined input to a defined output. A creative LUT adds a look. Convert first only when the look expects the converted image. A hybrid LUT can do both, so stacking another conversion may give the wrong result.
figureAlt: Matching source Apple ProRes Log and VideoFix Rec.709 SDR frames, showing normalization rather than a creative look.
figureCaption: Matched 2.000-second frames from an Apple ProRes Log source and its VideoFix SDR conversion. This demonstrates normalization, not a custom LUT or creative grade.
cards.technical.heading: Technical: change the encoding
cards.technical.body: Example: Apple Log to Rec.709. The expected camera curve and gamut matter. A Sony S-Log LUT does not become an Apple Log transform just because both images look flat.
cards.creative.heading: Creative: choose the appearance
cards.creative.body: A look may alter contrast, hues or saturation. It still expects a specific input. “Cinematic” is a style label, not an input color space.
cards.order.heading: Read the LUT’s input before choosing an order
cards.order.body: For a look designed for Rec.709, the simple chain is Apple Log → matching conversion → Rec.709 look. A look designed for Log belongs at a different stage. Check its documentation instead of assuming every creative LUT comes last.
cards.double-transform.heading: Why can two LUTs look worse?
cards.double-transform.body: Some LUTs combine normalization and a look. Feeding that hybrid LUT an already-converted image can exaggerate contrast or clip detail. An editor may also apply camera conversion automatically. Check both before adding another transform.

steps.input.text: In VideoFix: HDR Video Converter on iPhone, import Apple Log footage and open its Log preview. Import a compatible LUT. Select Original Log for an Apple Log-to-Rec.709 LUT; select Rec.709 when the LUT expects the normalized Rec.709 image.
steps.compare.text: Compare the same frame, especially bright clouds, skin and deep shadows. Export a short copy and play it back before processing a batch. A LUT is not a substitute for correcting an incorrectly exposed shot.
